title: Badminton: singles service
rulebook: BWF Laws of Badminton (BWF Statutes, Section 4.1, the edition in force in 2025): Law 1 (the court and the court equipment: 13.40 m x 6.10 m, 40 mm lines that are part of the area they bound, the singles side lines 5.18 m apart, the short service lines 1.98 m from the net; the net 1.524 m high at the centre and 1.55 m over the doubles side lines, 760 mm deep; the posts on the doubles side lines), Law 2 (the shuttle: 16 feathers, a cork base 25-28 mm across, 4.74-5.50 g), Law 3 (testing a shuttle for speed), Law 4 (the racket: at most 680 mm long and 230 mm wide), Law 9 (the service: 9.1 a correct service, 9.2 its start), Law 10 (singles: the service courts), Law 13 (faults)
deviations: Laws 7, 8, 10.2-10.3, 11 (the toss, the scoring, the rally, the receiver): one service only, with no receiver; a fault ends the attempt as a failure, a correct service that lands in the receiver's service court is the success; singles at the score 0 (so from the right service court, into the diagonally opposite one)
Law 9.1 (no undue delay; the receiver ready): there is no receiver; the service may come at any time within the episode

Law 9.2 (the start of the service is the first forward movement of the server's racket head once the players have taken their positions): taking position cannot be told from the robot's other arm movements; made measurable: a forward movement of the racket head starts when its speed towards the net rises above 0.5 m/s and lasts until that speed falls below 0.1 m/s; the service starts at the earlier of the release of the shuttle and the start of the head's forward movement that brings it to the hit; a forward movement of the head that starts after the release and stops before the hit is a fault (Law 9.1: the racket's movement continues forwards until the service is delivered)

Law 9.1 (some part of both feet in contact with the court in a stationary position): made measurable: from the start of the service to the hit each foot touches the floor (a gap of at most 0.02 s, the chatter of a contact, still counts as touching) and moves at most 0.03 m

Law 9.1 (the server lets go of the shuttle and hits it): the shuttle starts pinched by its feathers in the left hand's two-finger gripper and is let go by opening it; it counts as let go once it has touched nothing of yours for 0.03 s (the release is the moment it came free), so that the jaws' last brush as they open is part of the holding; so that the hand does not throw the service, the shuttle may move at most 4.0 m/s when it reaches the racket and must leave it faster than it came; one release per service (a shuttle that has been let go may be touched by nothing of yours but the racket)

Law 9.1 (the server's racket initially hits the base of the shuttle): judged at the physics step (1 ms) of the racket's first contact: the cork base must be touching the racket then (the feathers may touch it in the same step)

Law 9.1 (the server's racket): the racket must be held in the right hand throughout the attempt: it counts as held while it touches both jaws of the right gripper, and a break of at most 0.05 s (the contact chatter of a fast swing) is still held

Law 13 ('caught and held on the racket and then slung', 'hit twice'): made measurable: racket contacts less than 0.03 s apart are one hit, a later one is a second hit, and a contact longer than 0.02 s is a carry
Law 9.1 (the flight upwards from the racket): judged when the hit is over (0.03 s after its last contact): the shuttle is then rising
Law 13 (the shuttle landing outside the boundary lines; lines are in): the landing point is where the shuttle first touches the floor
Law 4 (the racket): a rigid racket (no string-bed deflection, no frame flex); its strings meet the shuttle with a restitution of 0.5
Law 1 (the net): a 2 cm thick wall instead of a mesh of cord; a shuttle that meets it is stopped by a stiff, strongly damped contact
the hall's air: still (no draught), at sea level and 15 C; the shuttle's spin about its axis is not driven by its feathers

texts.sentence: Serve: standing in your right service court, let the shuttle go from your left hand and hit it with the racket in your right hand, base first and below 1.15 m, over the net into the receiver's service court diagonally opposite.
texts.rules: The court is the BWF court: 13.4 m long and 6.1 m wide (between the doubles side lines), with the singles side lines 5.18 m apart, a short service line 1.98 m from the net on each side, a centre line from each short service line to the back boundary line, and a doubles long service line 0.76 m inside each back boundary line; every line is 0.04 m wide and is part of the area it bounds (the centre line is shared by the two service courts). This is singles: a service court reaches from the short service line to the back boundary line and from the centre line to the singles side line. The net stands across the middle, its top 1.524 m high at the centre and rising in a straight line to 1.55 m at the posts on the doubles side lines; it is 0.76 m deep, with open space under it. The shuttle is a feathered shuttle (5.1 g, a cork base 26 mm across, 16 feathers whose tips form a circle 64 mm across) with a shuttle's heavy air drag (it falls at 6.8 m/s at most) that turns it to fly cork first; it starts pinched by its feathers in your left hand's gripper, cork down. The racket (0.67 m, 85 g, strung area 0.27 m by 0.21 m) is held in your right hand's gripper by friction alone: it can slip, turn and fall. You serve from your right service court into the receiver's right service court, the one diagonally opposite. The racket must stay in your right hand all the time: it touches both of the gripper's jaws, and a break of more than 0.05 s is a fault. In order: (1) the release: your left hand lets the shuttle go; it is let go once it has touched nothing of yours for 0.03 s (the release is the moment it came free; until then it is still held), and from then on nothing of yours but the racket may touch it. (2) the hit: the racket hits the shuttle before it reaches the floor. At the first instant of contact the cork base is touching the racket (the feathers touching it first, alone, is a fault), the whole shuttle is lower than 1.15 m above the floor, the shuttle moves at most 4.0 m/s, and the racket head is moving towards the net. A forward movement of the racket head starts when its speed towards the net rises above 0.5 m/s and lasts until that speed falls below 0.1 m/s. The service starts at the earlier of the release and the start of the racket head's forward movement that brings it to the hit; a forward movement that starts after the release and stops before the hit is a fault. From the start of the service to the hit both feet stand in your service court, touching neither its lines nor anything outside it, each foot touching the floor all the time (a gap of at most 0.02 s still counts as touching) and moving at most 0.03 m. The hit is one contact: racket contacts less than 0.03 s apart are one hit, it lasts at most 0.02 s, and when it is over (0.03 s after its last contact) the shuttle is faster than it was when it reached the racket and is rising. (3) the shuttle passes the net's plane over the net's top edge, between the posts (it may touch the net). (4) its first contact with the floor (contacts less than 0.02 s apart are one) is inside the receiver's right service court, the lines included: that is the success. You fail on any fault: the shuttle reaching the floor, touching the net or passing the net's plane without a hit; the racket touching the shuttle before you let it go; the shuttle touching you, or touched by anything of yours but the racket, after the release; a hit that breaks a rule of (2); a second hit; a carry; the shuttle passing through or under the net or outside the posts, touching a post, landing on your side or outside that service court; the racket leaving your right hand, or touching the floor, the net or a post, at any time; any part of you touching the net or a post; a fall; or 15 s passing. A fall is: your pelvis lower than 0.35 m above the floor, or any part of you other than your feet touching the floor.
texts.venue: You stand in your right service court facing the net (+x), whose plane is 2.45 m ahead of your pelvis; the middle of the centre line is 0.45 m to your left, so your service court reaches from the near edge of the centre line to the outer edge of the singles side line 2.59 m to the right of the centre line's middle, and from the short service line (its edge nearest the net 1.98 m from the net) back to the back boundary line 6.70 m from the net. The receiver's right service court, your target, is beyond the net on the other side of the centre line: from 1.98 m to 6.70 m beyond the net, from the centre line to the singles side line 2.59 m to the left of the centre line's middle. Your forearms point forward; your left gripper's jaws pinch the shuttle's feathers, the shuttle hanging cork down; your right gripper's jaws clamp the racket's handle at its butt end, the handle along the fingers, the racket pointing forward and down from the hand, its strings facing the way the jaws close.
texts.difficulty: The shuttle must leave the strings at about 9 m/s or more, 40 to 55 degrees upwards, to clear a 1.52 m net 2 m away from a hit below 1.15 m, and the G1 meets it only in the lower part of a swing whose racket is held by friction in a parallel gripper; the left gripper's reach and the racket's path barely overlap, and the shuttle falls through it in a few hundredths of a second. The swing must leave the feet where they stand and the robot on them, on a stand without balance feedback.

stand.meaning: the platform holds the legs in the stance; you give the waist's 3 and the arms' 14 joint targets (rad) (grip_left: the left gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed); grip_right: the right gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed))

walk.meaning: Unitree's walking policy drives the legs from the velocity command (vx forward, vy to the left, m/s; wz turning left, rad/s; the robot's own frame); you give the waist and arm joint targets (grip_left: the left gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed); grip_right: the right gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed))

run.meaning: the running policy drives all 29 joints from the velocity command (it swings the arms) (grip_left: the left gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed); grip_right: the right gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed))

run_arms.meaning: the running policy drives the legs and the waist; you give the 14 arm joint targets (grip_left: the left gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed); grip_right: the right gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed))

joints.meaning: you give all 29 joint targets (rad); the default PD gains, no feed-forward (grip_left: the left gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed); grip_right: the right gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed))

lowcmd.meaning: Unitree's LowCmd for all 29 joints: position targets (rad), velocity targets (rad/s), feed-forward torques (N m), kp, kd; the motor torque is kp (q - q_measured) + kd (dq - dq_measured) + tau, evaluated at 1 kHz (grip_left: the left gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed); grip_right: the right gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed))

walk_falcon.meaning: FALCON's walking policy (LeCAR-Lab, trained with arm motions and forces on the hands; it also nudges the wrists) drives the legs from the velocity command (vx forward, vy to the left, m/s; wz turning left, rad/s; the robot's own frame); you give the waist and arm joint targets (grip_left: the left gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed); grip_right: the right gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed))

walk_agile.meaning: AGILE's velocity-height walking policy (NVIDIA WBC-AGILE, trained while the arms and the waist moved) drives the legs from the velocity command (vx forward, vy to the left, m/s; wz turning left, rad/s; the robot's own frame); you give the waist and arm joint targets (grip_left: the left gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed); grip_right: the right gripper's closure command, 0 (open, 90 mm) to 1 (closed))

robot.name: unitree_g1
robot.title: Unitree G1
robot.model: Unitree G1, 29 joints, 1.32 m, 34 kg (RoboOlympics robot library g1-4: MuJoCo Menagerie's unitree_g1 with Unitree's joint, speed and torque limits and motor torque-speed curves)

real_hands.model: Unitree Dex1-1 two-finger parallel gripper (modelled: 0.55 kg, jaws 80 mm long, 90 mm stroke, rubber pads)
real_hands.jaw_speed_note: the limit is the servo setpoint's; the jaws can move briefly up to about 0.45 m/s when a clamp springs open

servo.rule: each jaw: a setpoint moves towards 45 mm x closure at most half setpoint_opening_speed_m_s (opening, it starts from the jaws' position); force = clip(kp (setpoint - q) - kd dq, -force_limit_n, force_limit_n); the clamp on an object is min(force_limit_n, 10 N per mm that the commanded opening 90 mm x (1 - closure) is below the object's width)
